address.crossfade: When the track changes, the old one keeps playing until the new one has loaded. Then they crossfade over three seconds.
address.gesture: Browsers won’t start audio until the person has interacted with the page, so a `/play`{secondary} link opened from somewhere else lands on the track and waits for one click.
address.play: `/play`{secondary} at the end of a track’s address means it’s playing. Pause is a link back to the track. Skip links to the next one, which is picked as soon as the current track starts. Back and forward work, and a copied link opens the same track.

data.graphql: The original plan, while I was still using Audius, was to query GraphQL for the next track. That can come back if the catalogue grows.
data.route: This page doesn’t use GraphQL like the rest of the site. The catalogue is compiled into the page, and the audio comes from the storage bucket through the site’s `/assets/static`{secondary} route.

music.generated: Before that, the page generated its own music: a seeded synth playing chords and a melody over sampled piano. It was a lot of code to keep one station running, and I never got the piano samples into the bucket anyway, so I cut it.
music.hosting: I host them because a page can only analyse audio from its own origin, or from a server that explicitly allows it. Streamed from anywhere else, the tracks would play but the analyser would get nothing.
music.others: I looked at Audius and Jamendo first because their catalogues are much bigger. The machines I built this on couldn’t reach either service, so I went with a collection I could host myself.
music.source: The tracks come from [{{name}}]({{url}}): {{tracks}} tracks Bilal Tahir generated with Suno and released into the public domain. I copied them into the site’s storage bucket and serve them from there.

picture.analyser: For each frame, the page reads a few values from the audio analyser: overall energy, low, mid and high frequency energy, brightness, and whether a note just landed. It also passes the shader a {{bands}}-band spectrum as a texture.
picture.colours: The colours come from the stylesheet: six inks over a paper colour for each theme. A Bayer dither on top matches the rest of the site.
picture.dwell: A scene normally stays up for 24 to 38 seconds. If the music moves into a new section, it can change sooner, and the cut waits up to two and a half seconds for a note so it lands with the music.
picture.random: The next scene is random, and each track gets its own camera drift and a warmer or cooler lean. An earlier version picked scenes by genre. I dropped that because it was more code and the result didn’t look any better.
picture.shader: Everything on screen is drawn by one fragment shader. It has thirteen scenes (pools, clouds, rings, bars, a tunnel, a hive, a bloom and a few others) and blends between two at a time.

what_this_is.browser: The browser listens to the track, pulls a few numbers out of the audio and feeds them into a shader. There’s no machine learning and no server doing the work.
what_this_is.experiment: A small experiment I made for fun. The screen moves with whatever lo-fi track is playing.

error_playback: Could not play this track. Try again.
lede: {{tracks}} lo-fi tracks from a public-domain collection, each drawn while it plays in one of thirteen scenes. Press play once and it keeps going.
